title.narrative: Tanzania Cities Transforming Infrastructure & Competitiveness Project

description.narrative: The Tanzania Cities Transforming Infrastructure and Competitiveness Project will support urban development by strengthening urban management and improving access to basic infrastructure and services in participating urban areas in Tanzania. The theory of change underlying this project is that strengthening urban management will ensure the efficiency and sustainability of prioritized infrastructure and therefore enhance the productivity, livability, and resilience of strategically important cities in Tanzania. Urban management will be strengthened by leveraging ICT to enforce implementation of land use plans and increase own source revenue collection, using performance-based service management contracts operations and maintenance to improve service provision, in solid waste management, sanitation, and drainage. Strengthening urban management functions will require local governments taking on increasing responsibilities for the coordination of planning, implementation of plans, and operations and maintenance; and the national government providing policy and regulatory frameworks, supervision, monitoring, and enforcement. The project will implement basic infrastructure and services in participating urban local government authorities (LGAs) and improve the capacities of these local government institutions to plan, implement and maintain infrastructure and services in the longer term. There will be 45 local government authorities that will participate in the program. This includes those from the previous TSCP (8) and ULGSP (18) along with the inclusion of 19 new entities. All LGAs will receive institutional strengthening support under Component 1 and will be eligible for grants for infrastructure subprojects under Component 2. Subprojects may include urban roads, bus stands, markets, drainage, industrial cluster upgrades, public spaces and solid waste management, among others. Resources under Component 2 will be allocated according to LGA population, for which participating LGAs will be divided into three Tiers. The first, Tier 1 cities, consist of those with projected population of above 250,000 people by 2022 (next census) and population growth rates of above 15% percent. Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities will follow in subproject finalization and implementation. This approach ensures that infrastructure investments support the largest and fastest growing secondary cities in Tanzania while technical assistance activities continue to support other local authorities. Capacity of municipal governments to manage environmental and social issues will be considered in the selection process and technically supported as needed for selected municipalities.
To strengthen urban management performance and deliver improved basic infrastructure and services in targeted areas.

condition.narrative: Section I.A.1(a) of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:GoT to establish, within PO-RALG, by not later than sixty (60) daysafter effectiveness, and thereafter maintain throughout the period of implementation of the Project, a Project steering Committee,with a mandate, terms of reference, composition, and resources satisfactory to the Association, to provide policy guidance andhigh-level oversight in the carrying out of the Project,

Section I.A.1(b) of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:GoT to ensure that PO-RALG maintains a Project coordination team headedby a Project Coordinator and comprised of competent experienced, and qualified staff and/or consultants, in sufficient numbers andunder terms of reference acceptable to the Association, vested with financial resources, functions and competencies acceptable tothe Association, and set forth in the PIM, as shall be needed for the carrying out of the day-to-day implementation of the Project,

Section I.B.1 & 2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:GoT to prepare and adopt a Project implementation manual in a mannerand substance satisfactory to the Association, and thereafter implement and cause the selected participating LGAs to implement theProject (and in the case of the LGAs their respective subprojects) in accordance with such manual.

Section I.C.1 & 2 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:For purpose of Component 2 of the Project, GoT, through PO-RALG, to:(a) screen and select investments subprojects presented by selected participating LGAs pursuant to the eligibility criteria,assessment protocols and selection procedure acceptable to the Association, and set forth in Schedule 3 to the Financing Agreement,the ESCP and the PIM; and (b) enter into a subsidiary agreement with the respective LGA to facilitate part of the proceeds of thefinancing up to the amount authorized under the approved subproject, on terms and conditions acceptable to the Association and setforth in the PIM.

Section I.C.4 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:The selected participating LGAs (who have entered subsidiary agreements) toestablish and thereafter maintain a Project implementation team headed by a Project Coordinator and comprised of competentexperienced, and qualified staff and/or consultants, in sufficient numbers and under terms of reference acceptable to theAssociation, vested with financial resources, functions and competencies acceptable to the Association, and set forth in the PIM,as shall be needed for the carrying out of the day-to-day implementation of the respective subproject.

Section I.D.1 of Schedule 2 to the Financing Agreement:GoT to prepared and furnish to the Association, by no later than March 31of each year, an annual work plan and budget for the Project for the subsequent fiscal year, of such scope and detail as theAssociation shall have reasonably requested,
